key_insight: E-3DPSM introduces an event-driven state machine tailored to asynchronous, continuous event-camera streams that significantly improves monocular egocentric 3D human pose accuracy and latency compared to prior frame-oriented or naively aggregated approaches.
problem_solved: Existing egocentric 3D pose methods underutilize the asynchronous nature of event cameras, yielding insufficient accuracy and latency for immersive VR/AR and real-time applications; this work addresses how to process event streams natively to raise 3D estimation quality and responsiveness.
method: Design a state-machine architecture that consumes asynchronous event streams and emits timely pose updates by switching between event-aggregation, prediction, and refinement states.
Temporally-aware modules that fuse short-term event evidence with temporal priors/consistency to stabilize 3D pose regression from monocular head-mounted viewpoints.
Training and evaluation pipeline that optimizes accuracy and latency metrics for egocentric scenarios, demonstrating improved robustness to fast motions and challenging lighting.
impact: Makes event-camera-based egocentric 3D pose estimation practical for low-latency, high-dynamic-range applications (e.g., VR/AR, telepresence) by improving accuracy and responsiveness; provides a principled architectural pattern for future event-driven perception systems.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram of the E-3DPSM state machine showing states (aggregate → predict → refine) and asynchronous event input flowing through modules to produce 3D pose outputs.
Timing diagram that contrasts raw event stream processing vs. frame-based sampling, highlighting reduced latency and denser temporal updates.
Before/after qualitative poses: side-by-side 3D skeletons from prior methods and E-3DPSM on fast head motions and low-light scenes.
Bar/line chart comparing 3D pose error and end-to-end latency across baselines, showing accuracy and responsiveness gains.
paper_title: E-3DPSM: A State Machine for Event-Based Egocentric 3D Human Pose Estimation
paper_authors: Mayur Deshmukh, Hiroyasu Akada, Helge Rhodin, Christian Theobalt, Vladislav Golyanik
